title: Synthesis and Early Stage Sintering of Ultrafine HEA Nanoparticles
content: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are single-phase metallic materials composed of multiple elements in nearly equimolar ratios, gaining significant attention due to their unique chemical and physical properties. One of the most common processing routes for bulk HEAs is mechanical alloying; however, this method introduces contaminants, leading to the formation of undesirable oxides, nitrides, or carbides [2]. Meanwhile, chemical synthesis of HEA nanoparticles (HEA-NPs) has been widely explored for catalytic applications [3,4], demonstrating that HEA-NPs retain the same advantages as bulk HEAs while exhibiting increased surface area and higher surface energy [5]. Guo et al. developed a Fast Moving Bed Pyrolysis (FMBP) strategy to produce ultrasmall, highly dispersed, contaminant-free HEA-NPs comprising up to ten elements, ensuring high supersaturation of monomers and preventing phase separation [6]. This method allows mixed metal precursors to be simultaneously pyrolyzed at high temperatures, producing highly dispersed HEA-NPs supported on substrates. While FMBP is highly effective for nanoparticle synthesis, its potential for powder metallurgy remains unexplored. By controlling composition and processing conditions, FMBP may enable the development of bulk HEAs with novel microstructural features, such as nanograins, grain boundary segregation, and chemical composition influence on the atomic ordering. Additionally, the study of powder metallurgy of HEAs could advance applications in areas as additive manufacturing.
